What is an RCS agent?.summary: An RCS agent is the combination of two things: your verified brand (name, logo, business details) and one specific approved messaging purpose — e.g. marketing, customer support, or sales.

What is an RCS fallback message?.summary: The plain-text SMS version of an RCS message — like the plain-text version of an HTML email — sent (from a required fallback number) when the recipient can't receive RCS.

What carriers support RCS in the US?.summary: The three major US carriers supporting RCS are Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile (Apple, Google and the carriers worked together to enable it).

Does RCS work on iPhone?.summary: Yes — in September 2024, with iOS 18, Apple agreed to support Google's RCS technology, bringing RCS to iPhone.

What is the character limit for RCS mess.summary: RCS supports roughly 3,000 characters per message — far more than SMS's 160.

How many cards can an RCS carousel have?.summary: Up to 10 cards, each with its own image, buttons and call to action.

Can you send video in an RCS message?.summary: Yes — RCS messages can include video (e.g. inside stacked cards), which is new for text messaging.

What is conversation-based RCS pricing?.summary: Charging per conversation rather than per message — it exists in Europe, but in the US RCS is currently priced per message, not yet per conversation.

How long does RCS agent registration tak.summary: About 8 to 10 weeks (roughly a full quarter) to get approved.

What documents do you need to register a.summary: Your website and contact information, plus a privacy policy and terms & conditions that meet the approval requirements (similar to existing 10DLC/short-code registration), along with brand assets like a logo and banner.

Can one company have multiple RCS agents.summary: Yes — an agent is one brand + one use case, so a company can have multiple agents for different brands, locations, business units, or messaging purposes.

What is the difference between RCS and R.summary: RCS (Rich Communication Service) is the underlying messaging technology; RBM (RCS Business Messaging) is RCS used by a verified business sender to send branded business messages to customers/prospects.

How do you A/B test RCS messages?.summary: Use the analytics to compare creative — test different images (e.g. stock photo vs animation), carousel cards, and calls to action to see which gets the best response, then optimize.

Can RCS messages trigger calendar or pay.summary: Yes — RCS can interconnect with native phone apps: buttons can add to your calendar, start a call, or open Google Wallet to pay for something from within the messaging app.

What is 10DLC and why does it matter?.summary: A 10-digit long-code business number; it matters because carriers now require businesses to register their number and use cases via the Campaign Registry (a 'know your customer' process) so they know who's sending — each carrier (T-Mobile, AT&T, Verizon) has its own requirements.

What is the difference between a short c.summary: A long code is a standard 10-digit number (10DLC) that must be registered; a short code is a 5–6 digit number with a longer approval process but much higher throughput — better for mass, time-sensitive promotions.

How do I register a 10DLC campaign?.summary: TrueDialog has an automated 10DLC registration built into its platform — you fill out the application online (replacing the old paper/fax process) and they help ensure it adheres to carrier rules for approval.

What are TCPA compliance requirements fo.summary: For marketing/telemarketing texts you need prior express written consent: a clear, conspicuous disclosure (≈two sentences) that the person agrees to receive autodialed promotional messages, identification of the sender, and a statement that consent is not a condition of purchase — with affirmative opt-in (e.g. an unchecked checkbox).

How do I build an SMS subscriber list le.summary: Use explicit opt-in — e.g. a yes/no 'subscribe to marketing texts?' option on your forms — keeping marketing opt-ins separate from service messages.

How do I handle SMS opt-outs?.summary: Give a clear, easy opt-out (drive people to text STOP), use a platform that programmatically recognizes and honors STOP requests, and keep records of opt-ins and opt-outs.

What is an SMS fallback?.summary: The plain-text SMS version of an RCS message — like the plain-text version of an HTML email — automatically sent (from a required fallback number) when the recipient's device or carrier can't receive RCS.

How many characters can an SMS message b.summary: A standard SMS message is limited to 160 characters.

How do businesses use SMS for marketing.summary: For promotional campaigns, alerts, geolocation-based offers, and automated messages triggered by customer actions (order confirmations, appointment reminders) — often inside their marketing platform's journeys.

How can SMS improve sales pipeline?.summary: Add SMS steps to sales workflows so prospects who fill out a demo form, download content, or attend an event automatically get a personalized text; reps can also start 1:1 texts from a HubSpot contact record, all logged to the CRM.

What is the open rate of SMS vs email?.summary: Roughly: email ≈ 10% open rate over a couple of days, while SMS ≈ 95% open rate within 20 minutes (the speaker's working figures).

How do I use SMS for customer re-engagem.summary: Automate win-back texts at intervals after a customer lapses (e.g. 30/60/90 days after a gym cancellation) asking them to reply YES for a callback — recovering churned customers with no staff effort.

How do I measure the ROI of text message.summary: Use return on ad spend (ROAS) — the key metric for SMS since opens/clicks are harder to track. (Example: the Minnesota Wild estimated ~1,200% ROAS on a text campaign vs. a 'good' benchmark of 500–800%.)

How do I personalize SMS messages at sca.summary: Use templates and dynamic fields so each bulk text is customized, and target the right people with saved segments (e.g. HubSpot lists) — with opt-outs syncing automatically for compliance.

How do businesses use SMS for alerts and.summary: Send timed alerts that land on the recipient's home screen — e.g. the Minnesota Wild text fans ~2 hours before an event with 'know before you go' venue-policy info so they're not caught off guard.

How can companies use text messaging for.summary: Use two-way SMS for service — customers/students reply to texts, upload documents (transcripts, financial-aid forms), and resolve things quickly without phone tag or voicemail.

What is two-way SMS messaging?.summary: Messaging where recipients can reply, not just receive — e.g. send a text asking people to respond 'YES,' and their replies collect in a queue your team can act on, turning texting into a back-and-forth channel.

How does SMS work for appointment remind.summary: Appointment reminders are automated messages that can carry action buttons — check in, reschedule, or get directions/parking — so recipients act straight from the text. (Shown here as an RCS example rather than a dedicated SMS walkthrough.)

How do universities use text messaging t.summary: Across many departments — recruiting, help desk, library — because students respond to a text before email or a call (they always have their phone on them).

How do sports teams use SMS or RCS for f.summary: With RCS: deliver tickets straight to a wallet from one message, let fans pre-order concessions to their seat, send 'know before you go' info, and push game-day/championship merch with product photos.

How does SMS work in healthcare for pati.summary: Illustrated via a physical-therapy example: patient appointment reminders with check-in, reschedule, and directions/parking buttons — covered only lightly, as a hypothetical RCS use case rather than a dedicated healthcare segment.

How do financial services companies use.summary: Via API across their loan-management system, website and mobile app — triggering account alerts, sending MFA/2-factor codes, and running targeted bulk campaigns for customer reactivation (LCO Financial).

How can B2B software companies use SMS f.summary: Product-led software companies can nudge free or lower-tier users toward an upgrade — e.g. a free-trial-to-paid message prompting a self-service upgrade or a conversation with sales.

How does TrueDialog integrate with Sales.summary: A 100% native Salesforce integration — send bulk and two-way SMS directly from lead, contact, account and opportunity records, with all message activity logged natively in Salesforce.

How does TrueDialog integrate with HubSp.summary: A 100% native HubSpot integration — launch bulk SMS in seconds, personalize with templates/dynamic fields, and auto-sync opt-outs, extending HubSpot communications directly to SMS.

What analytics does TrueDialog's platfor.summary: Sent/delivered, replies, response time, typing indicators, SMS-fallback usage, segmentation for follow-up campaigns, A/B testing, and the ability to pull data into BI tools — richer than the basic sent/delivered/clicked of SMS/MMS.

How does TrueDialog handle compliance at.summary: Beyond carrier registration, its 'True Delivery' tool analyzes message templates against carrier spam filters and gives real-time, evidence-based feedback on whether a message will get flagged before sending to a large audience.

What makes an enterprise SMS platform di.summary: An enterprise platform is directly integrated with the carriers (first-party delivery) and bundles software + support, whereas many basic tools are just middleware handing messages to an aggregator (e.g. Twilio) — so the enterprise route removes a middleman and a point of failure.
